mainTopic: Fixing a wrongly done הולכה, and the מחלוקת of רבי שמעון and the רבנן about wrong thoughts during הולכה
overview: The גמרא asks whether a הולכה (carrying the blood to the מזבח) done the wrong way can be fixed by doing it again properly. A proof from the משנה about a כשר כהן handing blood to a פסול person is turned down. עולא then quotes רבי יוחנן that carrying without walking is פסול, which suggests it cannot be fixed. רב נחמן challenges this from the משנה about spilled blood that was gathered up and is כשר. The attempts to explain that משנה away fail, and עולא's rule is refuted: a bad הולכה can be fixed. Next comes a statement limiting the מחלוקת of רבי שמעון and the רבנן about wrong thoughts during הולכה. The scholars of ארץ ישראל laugh at it, and in the end the statement is flipped: everyone agrees about carrying by hand, and they argue only about carrying by walking. Finally, בני רבי חייא and רבי ינאי argue about a זר who carried the blood before a כהן carried it again. רב שימי בר אשי and רבא then discuss the reverse case, and רבא's reason continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Can a wrongly done carrying of the blood be fixed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a הולכה done in an invalid way can be corrected by doing it again properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible to fix it, or is it not possible to fix it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. The blood was carried toward the מזבח in a way that does not count. Can we bring it back and carry it again the right way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. Maybe the bad carrying just doesn't count, so we can redo it properly. Or maybe the bad carrying itself ruins the קרבן forever, so redoing it won't help.

keyTerms.meaning: carrying the blood toward the מזבח, one of the four main blood services

phrases.english: Is it possible to fix it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the carrying of the blood that was done the wrong way.

phrases.english: or is it not possible to fix it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקּוֹנַהּ אוֹ לָא אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקּוֹנַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a wrongly done הולכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an invalid הולכה can be fixed by redoing it properly, or whether it ruins the קרבן for good.

steps.title: A proof from the משנה: give the blood back to the fit כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a כשר כהן received the blood and gave it to a פסול person, and the blood should go back to the כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the fit one received the blood and gave it to the unfit one, he should return it to the fit one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a משנה. The blood is simply given back to the כשר כהן, so it seems the mistake can be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing the blood to a פסול person looks like an invalid carrying. Yet the משנה does not say the קרבן is ruined. It says to give the blood back to the כשר, which suggests a bad carrying can be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: fit: here, a כהן allowed to do the עבודה
unfit: someone not allowed to do the עבודה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
if the fit one received the blood and gave it to the unfit one,
he should return it to the fit one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That an invalid הולכה can be fixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: קבל הכשר ונתן לפסול יחזיר לכשר.

steps.title: Why taking the blood back proves it can be fixed
steps.stepSummary: Even if the משנה means the כשר takes the blood back himself, that only makes sense if the קרבן was not already ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if we say the fit one should go back and take it from him: if you think it cannot be fixed, the קרבן was already ruined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its proof stronger. However we read the משנה, it would be pointless to take the blood back if the קרבן were already ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the משנה only means the כשר כהן takes the blood back. That makes no difference. If a bad carrying could never be fixed, the קרבן would already be פסול the moment the blood reached the unfit person. Taking it back would accomplish nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: if it enters your mind / if you think

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. The גמרא is still building the same proof from step 2. It is just showing that the proof holds no matter how you read the word "return."

phrases.english: And even if we grant
that the fit one should go back and receive it from him,
if it enters your mind
that it is not possible to fix it,
it was already disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְהִי נָמֵי דְּיַחְזוֹר הַכָּשֵׁר וִיקַבְּלֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and strengthens the proof from the משנה in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That an invalid הולכה can be fixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the משנה lets the blood be taken back, which only works if the קרבן was not already ruined.

steps.title: The unfit person was standing farther from the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the משנה is talking about a זר standing outside, farther from the מזבח than the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think the non-כהן was standing inside, closer to the מזבח? No. He was standing outside, farther away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the משנה's case, handing the blood to the זר was not carrying it toward the מזבח at all, so there was no bad carrying to fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the זר stood between the כהן and the מזבח, which would make the handoff a real but invalid carrying. If the זר stood behind the כהן, the blood moved away from the מזבח. That is not a הולכה at all. So this משנה tells us nothing about fixing a bad הולכה, and the גמרא looks for another source in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: do you think? A formula that rejects an assumption

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails. If the זר stood farther from the מזבח, handing him the blood was not a carrying toward the מזבח, so there was nothing to fix. The גמרא keeps looking for an answer, and Step 11 settles it: a bad הולכה can be fixed.

phrases.english: Do you think
that the non-priest is standing inside?!
phrases.notes: "Inside" means between the כהן and the מזבח, so the handoff moved the blood toward the מזבח.

phrases.english: No, it is where the non-priest is standing outside.
phrases.notes: Here the blood moved away from the מזבח, so it was not a carrying toward the מזבח at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דְּקָאֵי זָר גַּוַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 2 and 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. The original question is taken up again in Step 5 and settled in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the זר stood closer to the מזבח. If he stood farther away, the handoff was not a הולכה at all.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: carrying the blood without walking ruins the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן that a הולכה done without walking is פסול. The גמרא learns from this that a bad הולכה cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: carrying the blood without walking is invalid. So it seems a bad carrying cannot be fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to answer our question: a wrong הולכה cannot be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן did not just say the carrying "does not count." He said it is פסולה, meaning the קרבן is ruined. If a second, proper carrying could fix it, he would not call it פסול. So the word אלמא draws the conclusion that there is no fixing.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was stated: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Carrying the blood not by foot is invalid.
phrases.notes: "Not by foot" means the כהן moves the blood toward the מזבח without walking, for example by stretching out his hand while standing still.

phrases.english: Apparently, it is not possible to fix it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source that seems to settle the question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הולכה done without walking makes the קרבן פסול, so a bad הולכה cannot be fixed.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges: spilled blood that was gathered up is כשר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a משנה: blood that spilled from the כלי onto the floor and was gathered up is כשר. This suggests a bad carrying can be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged עולא: If the blood spilled from the vessel onto the floor and he gathered it up, it is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks עולא's teaching from רבי יוחנן with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When blood spills and rolls along the floor toward the מזבח, it moves forward without anyone walking. That should be a הולכה שלא ברגל. Yet the משנה says that if you gather the blood, the קרבן is כשר, so it seems the bad carrying was fixed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman raised an objection to Ulla:
If it spilled from the vessel onto the floor
and he gathered it up, it is fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי יוחנן brought in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a bad הולכה cannot be fixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spilled blood rolling toward the מזבח is a carrying without walking, yet gathering it makes the קרבן כשר. So a bad carrying can be fixed.

steps.title: The blood spilled away from the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about blood that flowed outward, away from the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the blood went outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by saying the spilled blood moved away from the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הולכה means moving the blood toward the מזבח. If the blood rolled away from the מזבח, it was never a carrying at all, not even a bad one. So there was nothing to fix, and the משנה does not prove that a bad carrying can be fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a way of narrowing a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
Where it went outward.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spilled blood rolled toward the מזבח, which would be a bad הולכה that got fixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood rolled away from the מזבח, so no carrying happened at all and nothing needed fixing.

steps.title: Can spilled blood flow only outward?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: spilled liquid spreads in every direction, so how could it flow outward without also flowing inward?
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes outward but does not come inward?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the answer in step 7 is realistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When blood spills on a flat floor, it spreads to all sides. Some of it would surely move toward the מזבח, and that part would be a bad carrying. So the answer that it went only outward seems impossible.

phrases.english: It goes out outward, and does not come in inward?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָרַאי נָפֵיק לְגַוַּאי לָא עָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case the גמרא set up in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the blood flowed only away from the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spilled blood naturally spreads in every direction, so some would always flow toward the מזבח.

steps.title: Three cases where the blood would not spread toward the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three cases: the floor sloped away from the מזבח, the blood fell into a hole, or the blood was thick.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a place with a slope. Or, if you want, say: into a hole. Or, if you want, say: the blood was thick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three ways the blood could spill without moving toward the מזבח. This saves the answer from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case stops the blood from spreading inward. A slope makes it run only one way, a hole keeps it in one spot, and thick blood does not spread much. In all three, no carrying toward the מזבח happened, so רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another possible answer)
A hole or pit in the ground

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא defends רבי יוחנן: the משנה about spilled blood can be read as a case where the blood never moved toward the מזבח, because it ran down a slope, fell into a hole, or was too thick to spread. This defense is attacked in the next step, and עולא's rule is refuted in Step 11.

phrases.english: In a place with a slope.
phrases.notes: The floor slopes away from the מזבח, so the blood can only run outward.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: into a hole.
And if you wish, say: where it was thick.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְקוֹם מִדְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 and saves the answer of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the physical case, with three different possibilities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Spilled blood must spread toward the מזבח too.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a slope, a hole, or with thick blood, it does not spread inward at all.

steps.title: Would the משנה really teach such rare cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the three cases from Step 9. They are too rare, and the משנה could have made the distinction in a simpler place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Would the תנא really go to all that trouble just to teach us these rare cases? Also, in another chapter the משנה teaches that blood which spilled onto the floor and was gathered up is פסול. Instead, the משנה should have split the case of blood spilling from the כלי itself: it is כשר only if it flowed outward, but if it flowed inward it is פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from Step 9. It says the משנה would not hide its point in such strange cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two attacks. First, a sloped floor, a hole, or thick blood are rare cases, and a משנה would not quietly mean only those. Second, if the משנה really meant to split 'outward' from 'inward,' it would have said so openly. It had a natural place to do this, but it gave a different case of פסול instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it make a distinction in that very case
In what case is this said?

phrases.english: But did the תנא go to the trouble
to teach us all these?!
phrases.notes: 'All these' means the three rare cases from Step 9: a sloped floor, a hole, and thick blood.

phrases.english: And furthermore, rather than teaching in our other chapter:
if it spilled onto the floor and he gathered it, it is פסול;
phrases.notes: In that other case, the blood spilled straight from the animal's neck onto the floor, before it ever went into a כלי.

phrases.english: let it make a distinction within this case itself:
In what case is this said? When it went outward,
but if it came inward, it is פסול!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכְּפַל תַּנָּא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן כֹּל הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 9 as forced and unlikely
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (Steps 7 and 9) that the משנה about spilled blood is talking only about blood that flowed outward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה would not leave its key point hidden in rare cases. It would have stated the outward/inward distinction openly, and it had a natural place to do so.

steps.title: עולא's rule is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a full refutation of עולא's rule that a bad הולכה cannot be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no good answer left, so עולא's statement is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן said that carrying the blood without walking is פסול and cannot be fixed. The משנה about spilled blood shows it can be fixed, and the attempts to explain that משנה away have failed. So the conclusion is that a bad הולכה can be fixed by carrying the blood again properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the statement is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The final conclusion: a הולכה done the wrong way can be fixed. עולא's rule that it cannot be fixed is rejected.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: This knocks out עולא's rule from Step 5, that a bad הולכה can't be fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate after the answers of Steps 7 to 9 failed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A bad הולכה can be fixed. עולא's statement in the name of רבי יוחנן is refuted.

steps.title: The מחלוקת is only about a short hand-carrying
steps.stepSummary: A new statement limits the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the רבנן about wrong thoughts during הולכה. It applies only to carrying the blood by hand without walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: the מחלוקת between רבי שמעון and the רבנן is about carrying that is not done by walking. When the carrying is the 'big' kind, done by walking, everyone agrees that wrong thoughts make it פסול. They argue only about the 'small' kind of carrying, done by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement that narrows the famous מחלוקת about הולכה. Everyone agrees about walking, and they argue only about moving the blood by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brought a מחלוקת about whether a wrong thought during הולכה disqualifies the קרבן. This statement says that if the כהן walked with the blood, even רבי שמעון agrees the קרבן is פסול. The argument is only when the animal was killed right next to the מזבח and the blood was moved by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'small' carrying, done by moving the hand without walking

phrases.english: It was stated: carrying not by foot
is the dispute of רבי שמעון and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the מחלוקת in our משנה about whether a wrong thought during the carrying makes the קרבן פסול.

phrases.english: With regard to the greater carrying,
everyone agrees that it is disqualified;
where they disagree is the lesser carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: הוֹלָכָה שֶׁלֹּא בָּרֶגֶל מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after עולא's rule was refuted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the blood is carried by walking, everyone agrees that a wrong thought makes the קרבן פסול. רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue only about carrying the blood by hand without walking.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל mocks this with a bird חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל ask how a wrong thought could ever make a bird חטאת פסול according to רבי שמעון. There seems to be no moment when the thought would count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West: what about a bird חטאת, which can be made פסול by a wrong thought? According to רבי שמעון, how could that ever happen? If the כהן had the thought before the blood came out, it means nothing. If he had it after the blood came out, the מצוה was already done!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל challenge the statement of Step 12. They use a bird חטאת, whose blood goes straight from the bird's neck onto the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a wrong thought can make a bird חטאת פסול. But its blood is never carried by walking. Moving the bird is at most a 'small' carrying, and Step 12 says רבי שמעון ignores thoughts then. Once the blood is out, it is already on the מזבח and the מצוה is done, so there is no moment left for a thought to count.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at it; they found it very hard to accept
In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A bird חטאת, whose blood is sprinkled straight from its neck
A wrong thought or intention during the עבודה
Its מצוה has already been done

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: But a bird חטאת,
which a wrong thought disqualifies,
according to רבי שמעון, how can you find it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּחַשֵּׁיב עֲלַהּ מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִיפּוֹק דָּם –
phrases.english: If he had the thought about it before the blood came out,
it is nothing;
and if after the blood came out,
its מצוה was already done!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחֲכוּ עֲלַהּ בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement of Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון does not count a wrong thought during a 'small' carrying by hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, a bird חטאת could never become פסול through a wrong thought according to רבי שמעון. Before the blood comes out, the thought would not count, and after it comes out the מצוה is already done. Yet everyone accepts that a wrong thought does make it פסול.

steps.title: Maybe the thought counts while the blood is in the air
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the mockery. It suggests a wrong thought could count in the short moment between the blood leaving the bird and reaching the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe the thought counts from when the blood leaves the bird until it reaches the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question of ארץ ישראל. It points to a moment they missed. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars of ארץ ישראל said there were only two moments: before the blood came out, and after it landed. The גמרא suggests a third moment: while the blood is moving from the bird's neck to the מזבח. A wrong thought then could make the קרבן פסול even according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? This questions whether a challenge is real

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps from when it leaves the bird
until it reaches the מזבח –

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא מִדְּפָרֵישׁ וְעַד דִּמְטָא לְמִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the question of Step 13 by suggesting a moment it did not consider
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim of ארץ ישראל that there is no moment when a wrong thought could count for a bird חטאת according to רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question overlooked the moment while the blood is moving from the bird to the מזבח.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a moment the challenge overlooked (while the blood is in the air)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no moment when a wrong thought could make a bird חטאת פסול according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wrong thought could count while the blood travels from the bird to the מזבח, so Step 12's statement still stands.

steps.title: Proof from a priest whose hand was cut off mid-sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rules that if the sprinkler's hand is cut off before the blood reaches the airspace of the מזבח, the sprinkling is פסול. This shows the blood is still in the middle of the עבודה while it flies through the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: if a כהן was sprinkling and his hand was cut off before the blood reached the airspace of the מזבח, what is the law? He answered: it is פסול. Why? Because we need 'he shall sprinkle' to be like 'he shall place', meaning the blood must actually arrive at the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up Step 14 with a proof. The time between the blood leaving the bird and reaching the מזבח still counts as part of the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן becomes a בעל מום (his hand is cut off) while the blood is still flying, the הזאה is פסול. So the עבודה is not finished until the blood lands. That means a wrong thought in that moment could also make it פסול, which answers the question from Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: His hand was cut off (making him a blemished כהן)
'And he shall sprinkle... and he shall place' (ויקרא ד:ו-ז)

phrases.english: For indeed he asked of him
Rabbi Yirmeya, of Rabbi Zeira:
If he was sprinkling,
and the hand of the one sprinkling was cut off

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ דָּם לַאֲוִיר הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: before the blood reached the airspace of the altar,
what is the law? And he said to him: It is invalid.
What is the reason?
We require "and he shall sprinkle... and he shall place."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:6-7. The sprinkling has to end with the blood actually landing on the מזבח, like 'placing' it there.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of Step 14 with an earlier ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the moment between the blood leaving the bird and reaching the מזבח is still part of the עבודה and can be made פסול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's answer to רבי ירמיה: a sprinkler whose hand is cut off mid-sprinkle makes the הזאה פסול, based on 'והזה... ונתן'.

steps.title: The real reason for the laughter: the dispute is about walking
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא explain that the scholars laughed because the statement in Step 12 got it backwards. The מחלוקת is exactly about הולכה רבתי, not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע came from the בית מדרש, they said: this is why they laughed. Can it be that רבי שמעון and the רבנן do not argue about the 'big carrying' (walking)? That is exactly where they do argue!
steps.whatsHappening: A new explanation of the mockery from Step 13. It attacks the statement in Step 12 directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the מחלוקת is only about carrying by hand, and everyone agrees about carrying by walking. But רבי שמעון's whole reason is that הולכה can be skipped, and only walking can really be skipped. So the dispute must be about walking, and Step 12 is upside down.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Big carrying': carrying the blood by walking with it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same objection as Step 13. Step 13 asked about a bird חטאת. Here the problem is that Step 12's statement reversed the two kinds of carrying.

phrases.english: When Rav Pappa came

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, from the study hall,
they said: This is the laughter:
phrases.notes: They are explaining why the scholars of ארץ ישראל mocked the statement back in Step 13.

phrases.english: And about big carrying they do not argue?!
But when they argue,
it is about big carrying that they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתוֹ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב, אָמְרִי, הַיְינוּ חוּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside the bird discussion of Steps 13-15 and gives a new reason for the mockery, aimed at Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement in Step 12 that limits the מחלוקת to carrying by hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's reasoning (הולכה is skippable) only fits walking, so the dispute must be about הולכה רבתי, which is the opposite of what Step 12 said.

steps.title: The corrected version: everyone agrees about carrying by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the statement. With carrying by hand everyone agrees a wrong thought does not make it פסול. The dispute is only about carrying by walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: with 'small carrying' (by hand), everyone agrees it does not make the קרבן פסול. When they argue, it is about 'big carrying' (walking).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes Step 12 by reversing it, which answers the problem raised in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small movement by hand is not treated as the real הולכה, so no one says a wrong thought there makes it פסול. Walking with the blood is where they argue: רבי שמעון says it is skippable and a wrong thought does not make it פסול, and the רבנן say it does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Small carrying': moving the blood by hand without walking

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: הולכה by hand, everyone agrees it is not made פסול by a wrong thought. הולכה by walking, רבי שמעון says not פסול and the רבנן say פסול.

phrases.english: Rather, with small carrying,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא פָּסְלָה;
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it does not disqualify;
when they argue, it is about big carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּהוֹלָכָה זוּטַרְתִּי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא פָּסְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by reversing the statement of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the wording of the earlier statement (אלא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת is only about carrying by hand, and everyone agrees about walking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees that carrying by hand is not made פסול. The מחלוקת is only about carrying by walking.

steps.title: A non-priest carried the blood, and a priest brought it back and carried it again
steps.stepSummary: A זר carried the blood, then a כהן brought it back and carried it again. בני רבי חייא and רבי ינאי argue whether it is כשר, depending on whether a bad הולכה can be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a זר carried the blood, and a כהן brought it back and carried it again, the sons of רבי חייא and רבי ינאי argue. One says it is כשר and one says it is פסול. One holds a bad הולכה can be fixed, and one holds it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case with a מחלוקת. It returns to the question of whether a bad הולכה can be fixed, the idea behind עולא's rule from Step 5, which was refuted in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a wrong carrying is final or can be redone properly. The one who says כשר holds that the כהן's new carrying replaces the זר's carrying. The one who says פסול holds the first bad carrying already ruined the קרבן, which matches עולא's view even though it was refuted in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought it back to the starting place
It is possible to fix it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up Steps 19 and 20, where רב שימי בר אשי and רבא work out how each side of this מחלוקת rules in the reverse case.

phrases.english: If a non-priest carried it,
and a priest brought it back and carried it again,
there is a dispute about it
between the sons of Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yannai;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר כָּשֵׁר, וְחַד אָמַר פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: one says it is fit, and one says it is unfit.
One master holds: it is possible to fix it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the bad carrying. Can the כהן's new carrying make up for the זר's carrying?

phrases.english: and one master holds: it is not possible to fix it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלִיכוֹ זָר, וְהֶחְזִירוֹ כֹּהֵן וְחָזַר וְהוֹלִיכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wrong thoughts during הולכה to a new case about a זר doing the הולכה, connected to the question of fixing a bad הולכה (Step 11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: one says כשר because a bad הולכה can be fixed, and one says פסול because it cannot.

steps.title: The reverse case: the כהן carries first, the זר carries second
steps.stepSummary: A כהן carried the blood, brought it back, and then a זר carried it again. רב שימי בר אשי says the one who ruled כשר in Step 18 rules פסול here, and the one who ruled פסול there rules כשר here.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a כהן carried the blood toward the מזבח, brought it back, and then a זר carried it again: רב שימי בר אשי says that according to the one who called the earlier case כשר, this case is פסול. According to the one who called the earlier case פסול, this case is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case that is the mirror image of Step 18. רב שימי בר אשי explains how each side of that מחלוקת would rule here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the question was whether the first carrying counts for good, or whether a second carrying can replace it. If the second carrying is the one that counts, then here the second carrier was a זר, so it is פסול. If the first carrying is the one that counts, then here the first carrier was a כהן, so it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the blood to the מזבח, one of the four main steps of offering a קרבן
A non-כהן, who may not do the עבודה
He brought it back to its starting place
The one who rules it fit (כשר)
The one who rules it unfit (פסול)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases straight. In Step 18 the זר carried first and the כהן second. Here the כהן carries first and the זר second, which is why each opinion flips.

phrases.english: A priest carried it and brought it back,
and then a non-priest carried it again —
Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
According to the one who rules it fit, it is unfit;
phrases.notes: "The one who rules it fit" means the opinion that called Step 18's case כשר.

phrases.english: according to the one who rules it unfit, he rules it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלִיכוֹ כֹּהֵן וְהֶחְזִירוֹ, וְחָזַר וְהוֹלִיכוֹ זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the case from Step 18 and reverses who carried first and who carried second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each side of the Step 18 מחלוקת flips: the מכשיר there is פוסל here, and the פוסל there is מכשיר here.

steps.title: רבא says even the strict opinion rules it unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with half of רב שימי בר אשי's statement. He says even the one who ruled פסול in Step 18 rules פסול here, and he begins to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even according to the one who rules it unfit, it is unfit here. What is the reason? Because it is necessary...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the second half of רב שימי בר אשי's statement and starts to give his reason. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי בר אשי said the strict opinion would be lenient here, because a כהן did the first carrying. רבא says no, this case is פסול according to everyone. His reason begins with "because it is necessary," which shows that once the blood was brought back, something still had to be done with it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
even according to the one who rules it unfit, it is unfit;
What is the reason?
Because it is necessary

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אַף לְדִבְרֵי הַפּוֹסֵל פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רב שימי בר אשי's statement in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that the פוסל of Step 18 would rule כשר in the reverse case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: After the blood was brought back, it still needed to be carried again, so the זר's carrying cannot be ignored. The full reason is finished on the next עמוד.
